tone_statements.citation: Ibrahim, Sjahrial S. A. R., Rustam Effendi & M. P. Lambut. 1991. Struktur Bahasa Bosap. Jakarta: Departemen Pendidikan dan Kebudayaan. xv+144 pp.
tone_statements.quote: 3.8 Fonem Suprasegmental. Fonem suprasegmental tidak terdapat dalam bahasa Bosap. Tekanan [s] (stress), nada (pitch), panjang pendek (quantity), dan jeda (pause) tidak membedakan arti suatu kata. Kata [nipa] 'ular' dengan tekanan pada suku pertama dari belakang tidak berbeda artinya dengan tekanan pada suku ke dua dari belakang /nipá/
tone_statements.translation: 3.8 Suprasegmental phonemes. There are no suprasegmental phonemes in Bosap. Stress, pitch (tone), length (quantity) and pause do not distinguish the meaning of a word. The word [nipa] 'snake' with stress on the last syllable does not differ in meaning from [nipa] with stress on the second syllable from the end /nipá/.
tone_statements.locator: Bab III Fonologi, section 3.8 'Fonem Suprasegmental', pp. 23-24; restated in Bab VI, 6.1 Kesimpulan, p. 124 item f: 'Fonem suprasegmental tidak dijumpai dalam bahasa Bosap.'
tone_statements.summary: No tone: pitch is explicitly non-phonemic (as are stress, length and pause); Basap/Bosap is described as lacking suprasegmental phonemes altogether.

In I Wayan Arka, Ni Luh Nyoman Seri Malini & Ida Ayu Made Puspani (eds.), Language documentation and cultural practices in the Austronesian world: Papers from 12-ICAL, Volume 4, 149-177. Canberra: Asia-Pacific Linguistics (ANU).
sources.note: Nothing. The chapter (pp. 149-177, Lebbo' = a Basap variety of the Lesan/Kelai area, Berau) is ethnohistory plus lexical comparison tables and morphology notes; the only phonological remark is footnote 4 (p. 153): 'the phonology of Lebbo'.. does not exhibit specific features.. orthographic symbols correspond to phonemic notation in IPA' (orthography key). No mention of stress, accent, or syllable prominence anywhere in the chapter.

sources.note: The only phonology-bearing description of Basap (Wikipedia's consonant and vowel tables are drawn from it). Pusat Bahasa 'Struktur Bahasa' sketches almost always have a 'Tekanan' (stress) subsection in the phonology chapter, so this is the most likely place for a word-stress statement. Describes the Bosap of Jitan village, Loa Kulu, Kutai.

The word [nipa] 'snake' with stress on the last syllable does not differ in meaning from [nipa] with stress on the second syllable from the end /nipá/.

tone.says: First-hand statement (Pusat Bahasa field sketch, Loa Kulu Bosap) that the language has no suprasegmental phonemes: pitch/tone, stress, length and pause are all non-distinctive; illustrated with [nipa] 'snake' pronounced with final or penultimate stress without change of meaning. The phonology chapter (pp. 15-25) otherwise gives consonant, vowel and diphthong inventories, distribution, syllable structure and phonological rules; no tone marks anywhere in the data or texts.
